Here’s a highly advanced Keras project—an end-to-end pipeline for unsupervised multivariate time-series anomaly detection using an Attention-powered ConvLSTM Autoencoder with Dynamic Thresholding, inspired by ACLAE‑DT (mdpi.com).

Project Title

ai-ml-ds-YZ3kLpQwRf1
Filename: attention_convlstm_autoencoder_dynamic_threshold.py

📌 Short Description

Build an unsupervised anomaly-detection system for multivariate time-series. It constructs correlation-image “feature maps” per sliding window, trains a ConvLSTM autoencoder with attention to reconstruct those maps, and applies dynamic thresholding on reconstruction errors to flag anomalies.

🧠 Problem Domain

Multivariate time-series anomaly detection—key for manufacturing, IoT, finance, or healthcare systems.

⚙️ Frameworks

  • TensorFlow / Keras (2.0+)
  • scikit-learn
  • numpy, pandas

🚀 Project Code

# attention_convlstm_autoencoder_dynamic_threshold.py

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import MinMaxScaler
from tensorflow.keras import layers, Model, Input
import tensorflow as tf
import datetime

# timestamp
print("Timestamp:", datetime.datetime.now())

def load_data() -> pd.DataFrame:
    from sklearn.datasets import load_boston
    data: np.ndarray = load_boston().data  # using Boston for placeholder: real should be multivariate TS
    df: pd.DataFrame = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=load_boston().feature_names)
    return df

def create_feature_images(df: pd.DataFrame, window: int = 10) -> np.ndarray:
    arr: np.ndarray = df.values
    N, D = arr.shape
    images = []
    for i in range(N - window + 1):
        block: np.ndarray = arr[i:i+window]
        corr: np.ndarray = np.corrcoef(block, rowvar=False)
        images.append(corr[..., np.newaxis])
    return np.array(images)  # shape: (samples, D, D, 1)

def build_model(input_shape):
    inp = Input(shape=input_shape)  # (D, D, 1)
    x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv2D(32, (3,3), activation='relu', padding='same'))(inp)
    x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.MaxPooling2D((2,2), padding='same'))(x)
    x = layers.ConvLSTM2D(16, (3,3), activation='relu', padding='same', return_sequences=False)(x)
    # attention mechanism
    att = layers.Flatten()(x)
    att = layers.Dense(np.prod(x.shape[1:]), activation='softmax')(att)
    att = layers.Reshape(x.shape[1:])(att)
    x = layers.multiply([x, att])
    # decoder
    x = layers.Conv2DTranspose(32, (3,3), strides=(2,2), activation='relu', padding='same')(x)
    out = layers.Conv2D(1, (3,3), padding='same')(x)
    model = Model(inputs=inp, outputs=out)
    model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='mse')
    return model

def dynamic_threshold(errors: np.ndarray, factor: float = 3.0) -> float:
    mu: float = np.mean(errors)
    sigma: float = np.std(errors)
    return mu + factor * sigma

def main():
    df: pd.DataFrame = load_data()
    scaler = MinMaxScaler()
    arr_norm = scaler.fit_transform(df)
    df_norm: pd.DataFrame = pd.DataFrame(arr_norm, columns=df.columns)
    window: int = 20
    feature_images: np.ndarray = create_feature_images(df_norm, window)  # shape = (samples, D, D, 1)
    X: np.ndarray = np.expand_dims(feature_images, axis=1)  # add time axis: (samples, 1, D, D,1)

    split = int(0.7 * len(X))
    X_train, X_test = X[:split], X[split:]
    model: Model = build_model(X_train.shape[1:])
    model.fit(X_train, X_train.squeeze(), epochs=30, batch_size=16, validation_split=0.1)

    recon_train: np.ndarray = model.predict(X_train)
    train_err: np.ndarray = np.mean((X_train.squeeze() - recon_train)**2, axis=(1,2,3))
    thresh: float = dynamic_threshold(train_err)
    print("Dynamic threshold:", thresh)

    recon_test: np.ndarray = model.predict(X_test)
    test_err: np.ndarray = np.mean((X_test.squeeze() - recon_test)**2, axis=(1,2,3))
    anomalies: np.ndarray = np.where(test_err > thresh)[0]
    print("Anomaly indices in test set:", anomalies)

    # Examples
    for idx in anomalies[:5]:
        print(f"Index {idx} error={test_err[idx]:.4f} > threshold")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

  • Feature-image construction from correlations
  • ConvLSTM + attention in encoder-decoder
  • Dynamic thresholding for anomaly detection
  • Sliding-window feature extraction

✅ Final Product

An automated pipeline that extracts sliding-window correlation-image features, reconstructs them via an attention‑ConvLSTM autoencoder, computes reconstruction error online, and flags anomalies that exceed a dynamic threshold.

  • Real-time streaming inference
  • Multi-scale windowing and hierarchical attention
  • Sparse labeling + weak supervision
  • Explainability: highlight which sensor pair correlations triggered anomaly
